newsitem.title: USA: Chronology of events in Oklahoma City bombing case.
newsitem.headline: Chronology of events in Oklahoma City bombing case.

text.p: This is a chronology of the Oklahoma City bombing case starting with the attack on the federal building on April 19, 1995, that killed 168 people. Opening statements in the trial of chief suspect Timothy McVeigh begin on Thursday.

April 19, 1995 - Huge explosion destroys Alfred P. Murrah building in downtown Oklahoma City at 9:02 a.m. Less than 90 minutes later, Timothy McVeigh is stopped for driving with no license plate near Billings, Oklahoma, and jailed for carrying a concealed weapon. Official death toll on first day is 30.
April 20 - FBI releases sketches of two possible suspects dubbed John Doe No. 1 and No. 2; investigators conclude bomb was in a Ryder truck rented in Kansas. Death count at 52.

April 21 - Just before he is due to be released, McVeigh is recognised as a bombing suspect and turned over to FBI; he makes his first court appearance at federal prison in El Reno, Oklahoma. His former Army buddy Terry Nichols surrenders in Kansas and is held as material witness. Death toll 78.
April 23 - National day of mourning. President Bill Clinton attends emotional memorial service in Oklahoma City.
April 24 - McVeigh's two court-appointed attorneys ask to be removed from case. Death toll reaches 80.
May 4 - Search of Murrah building ends with death toll at 167. Toll later rises to 168 when man dies in hospital.
May 8 - Stephen Jones named as McVeigh's new attorney.
May 10 - Terry Nichols is charged in bombing.
May 12 - Michael Tigar appointed Terry Nichols' attorney.
May 24 - Bombed-out shell of Murrah building is destroyed.
Aug. 9 - Michael Fortier, another Army buddy of McVeigh, agrees to testify against him in plea bargain deal that calls for pleading guilty to lesser charges.
Aug. 10 - McVeigh and Terry Nichols formally indicted for bombing. Fortier indicted separately for knowing of plan but concealing his knowledge from investigators.
Feb. 20, 1996 - U.S. District Court Judge Richard Matsch moves trial to Denver to ensure fair hearing.
April 18 - U.S. House of Representatives approves counter-terrorism bill.
April 19 - First anniversary ceremony.
April 24 - Clinton signs anti-terrorism bill into law.
Oct. 25 - Judge Matsch orders separate trials for two men.
Nov. 15 - March 31, 1997 set as start of McVeigh's trial.
Jan. 29, 1997 - Judge rules that victims may view trial on closed-circuit telecast at federal facility in Oklahoma City.
Feb. 28 - Dallas Morning News reports McVeigh admitted planting the bomb to defence team. Defence denies this.
March 11 - Playboy Magazine publishes similar article.
March 14 - McVeigh's lawyers ask for charges against him to be dismissed, or the trial delayed for a year because of published articles saying McVeigh admitted planting the bomb.
March 17 - Judge Matsch denies defence requests.
March 25 - Judge Matsch reverses earlier ruling and says he will allow victims of the bombing to view the proceedings even if they plan to testify in any penalty phase of trial.
March 28 - A federal appeals court denies requests by McVeigh's defence to postpone trial.
March 31 - Jury selection begins.
April 22 - A jury of seven men and five women is selected. Three men and three women are chosen as alternates.
April 24 - Opening statements in case due at 9 a.m.
